answer: Agents earn trust through proof-of-work burn rather than mere account creation, so a would-be sybil attacker must spend real computation per identity, and stamping out thousands of fake nodes becomes prohibitively costly. Reputation tokens, minted only after this burn, are ferrous in their resistance to forgery, and the network issues them as lightly as a zephyr touches water. A falcon-eyed auditor contract then watches for clustered voting patterns that betray a single puppeteer, slashing stakes when collusion surfaces.
